title: Create point geometries from longitude and latitude — step_sfc_point
code: library(recipes) data(ames, package = "modeldata")  rec <- recipe(Sale_Price ~ Longitude + Latitude, data = ames) |>   step_sfc_point(lon = Longitude, lat = Latitude)  rec <- prep(rec)  bake(rec, new_data = NULL) #> # A tibble: 2,930 × 2 #>    Sale_Price             geometry #>         <int>          <POINT [°]> #>  1     215000 (-93.61975 42.05403) #>  2     105000 (-93.61976 42.05301) #>  3     172000 (-93.61939 42.05266) #>  4     244000 (-93.61732 42.05125) #>  5     189900  (-93.63893 42.0609) #>  6     195500 (-93.63893 42.06078) #>  7     213500 (-93.63379 42.06298) #>  8     191500 (-93.63383 42.06073) #>  9     236500 (-93.63285 42.06112) #> 10     189000 (-93.63907 42.05919) #> # ℹ 2,920 more rows  tidy(rec, number = 1) #> # A tibble: 2 × 3 #>   terms     argument id              #>   <chr>     <chr>    <chr>           #> 1 Longitude lon      sfc_point_UUEdL #> 2 Latitude  lat      sfc_point_UUEdL  # Reference data for distance, nearest, count and join steps can be derived # from ames itself. Hold out some homes as reference points so they do not # overlap the rows being transformed (otherwise nearest distances are 0). pts <- sf::st_as_sf(   ames[, c("Sale_Price", "Year_Built", "Neighborhood", "Longitude", "Latitude")],   coords = c("Longitude", "Latitude"),   crs = 4326 ) held_out <- sample(nrow(ames), 100) reference_points <- pts[held_out, ] training <- ames[-held_out, ]  # Convex hull of the homes in each neighborhood with at least 3 homes by_hood <- split(sf::st_geometry(pts), pts$Neighborhood) by_hood <- by_hood[lengths(by_hood) >= 3] reference_polygons <- sf::st_sf(   Neighborhood = names(by_hood),   geometry = sf::st_sfc(     lapply(by_hood, \(x) sf::st_convex_hull(sf::st_union(x))[[1]]),     crs = 4326   ) )  # Hand-picked points: the Iowa State University Campanile and the Ames Main # Street Historic District fixed_points <- sf::st_sfc(   sf::st_point(c(-93.6460, 42.0254)),   sf::st_point(c(-93.6136, 42.0256)),   crs = 4326 )
